wrought_pure_and_1xxx: Generally strong atmospheric corrosion resistance due to protective oxide film; aggressive environments can still cause localized attack.
2xxx: Copper-bearing alloys generally have lower corrosion resistance than 5xxx/6xxx families and commonly require protection in demanding environments.
5xxx: Generally good corrosion resistance, especially in marine environments, but sensitization/intergranular corrosion can matter for certain compositions, thermal histories and service conditions.
6xxx: Generally good corrosion resistance with broad engineering utility.
7xxx: High-strength grades can be more environmentally sensitive; stress-corrosion and exfoliation behaviour must be assessed against exact temper/product form.
cast_and_am: Porosity, microstructure, surface condition and process history can materially affect corrosion performance.
galvanic: Aluminium is relatively anodic; dissimilar-metal coupling in electrolyte requires galvanic compatibility assessment.
hydrogen: Hydrogen effects are not represented as a universal alloy property; assess where process/service charging and fracture consequences make it relevant.
